newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat meets Ross, Israeli officials.
newsitem.headline: Arafat meets Ross, Israeli officials.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat met Israeli government officials on Sunday for the first time since an Islamic militant suicide bombing on an Israeli market threw peace moves into deeper crisis.

A Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) official told Reuters U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross brought Israeli negotiator Yitzhak Molho and Shin Bet secret police chief Ami Ayalon with him to a meeting with Arafat in Ramallah.
"The meeting is focussing on security and political issues but mainly on security issues," said the PLO official, who spoke on condition he not be named.
Ross's delegation travelled to Ramallah from Jerusalem where Ross had just ended his second meeting of the day with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Israel insists Ross's present mission is confined to security concerns. Arafat, who also was meeting Ross for the second time in a day, pointedly told reporters after his first meeting with Ross that "talks were not confined to security matters".

Peacemaking between the sides, already in crisis over Israel beginning a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March, hit a new low on July 30 when two Islamic militant suicide bombers killed 13 people at a Jerusalem market.
